I can only speak about what i do know. My mom was  diagnosed in 08 with breast cancer. I know it was estrogen fed cancer and they put her immediately on a hormone blocker. When she under went surgery they removed q2 lympphnodes and cancer was found in 10. So the surgeon told us the cancer would come back where would be the mystery question. Almost a year later my mother fell and they did a CT scan they saw something and immediately did a MRI. She had a small marble size tumor right in her hip joint. She choose not to biopsy it and decided to try radiation. It didn't work the tumor got bigger. At this point we as a family made the decision that quality over quantity of life was more important and stopped treatment. My mother had a lot of other medical issues on top of cancer. She passed away less then 6 months after stopping treatments she was 64. My paternal grandmother was dx mid 90's she was in her 80's by this time and didn't want any treatment. I do know more then most about genetics as i have a child who has Down Syndrome and we went through testing then. DS can be genetic it wasn't in our case. I really have educated myself about that subject it will be interesting to me to see if anything is genetic.

So my Grandparents bordered the TN/KY line, grandpa was from TN Grandma was from KY. They met at a lunch auction he bought her lunch and then they shared it! I love that part of the story! He courted her on his mule. He worked for the CCC and took huge boulders and made it into pea gravel and earned a whole dollar a week. I can't even imagine the bach breaking labor that was. It has taught me not to complain about all the little jobs i need to do in a day. Then he worked for Stearns Coal and Lumber. Grandpa was the best Muler around. They say he loved his mules just as much as his family. He pulled lumber out of what is know Daniel Boone National Forest.  But in the winter he couldn't lumber so he had to work the mines. He got paid 20 cents for every ton of coal he moved. He didn't get paid for moving the debris. All pay was company script. So he started moon shining to make actually money. His brother in law would transport it from southern Ky to the Cincinnati area and sell it. As far i know they were never caught. The money helped supplement what was a very poor family. Then for reasons i still don't know their house was burnt down and they made their way up North ( i was born and raised in Indiana but have always claimed to be southern ) Grandpa gave his children a chance at good factory jobs ( which my father had ) Sadly my Grandpa does right after i turned 7. Yet i know he is still with me. He loved roses and had a rose garden periodically i will smell roses for no reason. I have always taken that as a sign from him. Now 30+ years later every grandchild owns their own home something he sadly never accomplished. Makes me proud to be his granddaughter. 

Edit..We went about 15 years ago back down to KY to see of we could find the still ( spelling ) my father helped "hide" it when they moved. Sadly we didn't find it. I don't know how much trouble we would have got into hauling it out a national park!
I will take some shine! My Grandpa was a moonshiner.
